title: Verified Facts Must Govern Vietnam’s Dog-Trade Reform
excerpt: Rabies can kill after symptoms begin, while stolen-pet and transport claims require proof. Vietnam needs transparent enforcement and abolition by 2030.
body_html:
Rabies leaves no room for complacency: once clinical symptoms appear, disease is virtually 100% fatal. Possible exposure demands immediate wound washing with soap and running water for at least 15 minutes, followed by urgent medical assessment and post-exposure prophylaxis when indicated. World Health Organization guidance makes this plain.

Myths cannot replace records

“Tradition” does not prove safe sourcing. “Farm-raised dogs” does not prove lawful transport, veterinary inspection, vaccination, or traceability. Claims about cyanide bait, stolen pets, syndicate convictions, specific seizures, and unquarantined shipments require police records, court judgments, inspection reports, or named official statements. None are supplied here. No honest campaign should turn unverified allegations into fact.

Biosecurity needs proof and enforcement

Rabies exposure can involve infected saliva entering bites, scratches, broken skin, or mucous membranes. Handling sick animals, uninspected slaughter, and bite attacks create risks. Properly cooked meat is not an established rabies transmission route. Household exposure incidents and commercial supply chains are separate dimensions of biosecurity failure; one must not be falsely presented as causing the other.

Vietnamese families, veterinarians, officials, and animal-protection leaders can demand records, quarantine compliance, humane enforcement, and protection for companion animals. Public-health targets set by state authorities are not the same as SDE’s campaign demand: complete abolition of the dog-meat trade by 2030.

Demand a lawful end

Sign SDE’s national petition calling for nationwide abolition by 2030. Add your name to a public demand for action, and follow campaign updates on how that demand reaches decision-makers.
